name: Renal Medullary Carcinoma
aliases: Renal Medullary Carcinoma of the Kidney

criteria.description: Histopathologic identification of poorly differentiated carcinoma with reticular or cribriform architecture in the renal medulla
Presence of sickle cell trait or disease confirmed by hemoglobin electrophoresis
Loss of SMARCB1 (INI1) expression on immunohistochemistry
Imaging showing centrally located renal mass with infiltrative growth pattern

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathologic confirmation of tumor in renal medulla with loss of SMARCB1 expression and presence of sickle cell trait or disease
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on histopathology and immunohistochemistry in the context of clinical and radiologic findings.

pathognomonic.notes: Common presenting symptom due to tumor invasion

pathognomonic.symptomName: Flank mass palpable on physical examination
Severe flank pain localized to affected kidney

searchTerms: high blood pressure from kidney disease
renal involvement leading to high blood pressure

occasional.symptomName: Lower extremity edema due to venous obstruction
searchTerms: lower limb edema due to venous obstruction
swollen legs from blood flow blockage
low red blood cells from chronic illness
chronic disease causing low blood count
microscopic blood in urine before visible bleeding
shortness of breath from lung tumors

rare.symptomName: Spinal cord compression from vertebral metastases
searchTerms: spinal cord pressure from bone tumors

laboratory: Hemoglobin electrophoresis positive for sickle cell trait or disease
imaging: CT or MRI showing centrally located infiltrative renal mass in medulla
genetic: Loss of SMARCB1 (INI1) tumor suppressor gene expression
No common mutations seen in other renal cell carcinomas
other: Histopathology showing poorly differentiated carcinoma with reticular or cribriform pattern

distinguishingFeatures: Collecting duct carcinoma typically occurs in older patients
Lacks association with sickle cell trait
Different immunohistochemical profile with retained SMARCB1 expression
Clear cell RCC usually arises from renal cortex, not medulla
No association with sickle cell trait or loss of SMARCB1

redFlags: Rapidly progressive flank mass with hematuria in young patient of African descent
Presence of sickle cell trait with aggressive renal tumor
Loss of SMARCB1 expression on tumor biopsy
references: Srigley JR, Delahunt B. Renal Medullary Carcinoma. WHO Classification of Tumours of the Urinary System and Male Genital Organs. 2016.
Swartz MA, Karth J, Schneider DT, et al. Renal medullary carcinoma: clinical, pathologic, immunohistochemical, and genetic analysis with pathogenetic implications. Urology. 2002.
Agarwal PK, et al. Renal Medullary Carcinoma: A Review. Oncologist. 2019.
